patch.value: Baseline measured 2026-07-29 across one source file (index.ts): 91.21 line, 77.36 branch, 93.07 function. Thresholds are pinned at the measured floor (91/77/93) so the number can only move up.
Enforce a real coverage gate by running tests against TypeScript sources

The package measured no coverage at all: tests imported the compiled output from dist, so the only obtainable numbers pointed at generated JavaScript offsets an author cannot act on, and no threshold was wired into any gate. The suite now runs against the TypeScript sources directly. Node executes TypeScript natively from the version floor this package already declares, so tests import the source module, which puts the coverage report on real source lines. The gate is scripts/coverage-gate.ts: it enforces per-dimension thresholds and reconciles the reported file list against a walk of the source tree. That second check is the point. Node omits files that never load from its report entirely rather than reporting them at zero, so without it a package can satisfy a full threshold while an entire module goes unexercised.

Tests import TypeScript sources rather than dist so coverage reports on editable lines; the gate fails the build when any threshold regresses; the gate fails when a source file never loads, proven by a negative control; thresholds are recorded in package.json as a ratchet at the measured baseline; the gate runs in the release check and in CI on Node 22 and 26.
A coverage gate runs in the release check and in CI on both supported Node lines, reports against TypeScript sources, and fails when a source file is untested or a threshold regresses.
